title: Sumac-mediated green synthesis of highly active ZnO nanoparticles as sustainable photocatalyst material with efficient methylene blue dye degradation properties
content: In the present study, an eco-friendly method for the synthesis of ZnO nanoparticles was demonstrated using the extract of Rhus coriaria (sumac) and photocatalytic activity in dye treatment was studied. Systematic study of the effect of post-synthesis calcination at 300, 500, and 700 °C on structural, optical, morphological and photocatalytic behavior of the resultant ZnO nanoparticles has been performed. The characterizations verified the formation of phase-pure hexagonal wurtzite ZnO with quasi-spherical nanoparticles having average particle sizes of 21–30 nm. The XRD-derived crystallite sizes were 5.10, 4.92, and 10.42 nm for ZnO-300, ZnO-500, and ZnO-700, respectively, while the corresponding lattice microstrain values were 2.19 × 10−2, 2.27 × 10−2, and 1.06 × 10−2. The evolution of the structural properties and optical properties were found to be strongly dependent on the calcination and were estimated as 4.43 eV for ZnO-300, 3.12 eV for ZnO-500 and 2.83 eV for ZnO-700. In the investigated conditions, the ZnO-500 sample at a loading of 1.17 g L−1 with a final degradation efficiency of 97.5% and a relatively high apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant (0.02080 min−1) showed the highest efficiency of MB degradation. The optimized sample of ZnO-500 had a high negative ζ potential of −57.1 mV and high specific surface area of 11.2 m2 g−1. The results of the trapping experiments with reactive species, with scavenger only control experiments, and with the pH monitoring were consistent with the possible involvement of pathways related to photogenerated holes and hydroxyl-radicals; however, these results are not sufficient to establish the pathway. The degradation efficiencies of ZnO-500 were also greater than 93% at the first 4 reuse cycles. In conclusion, the results have shown that the green-synthesized ZnO presented significant influence of calcination temperature on the structural, optical, morphological and surface characteristics, and the photocatalytic performance was a result of a combination of these properties, not just crystallinity, optical band gap or an inferred defect mechanism.
